answer: An agent economy can blunt sybil attacks by pricing identity in work rather than signups: each new agent must post collateral and clear a probationary queue of tasks that require distinct, verifiable execution, so one operator cloning a thousand profiles pays a thousand times. Duplicate fingerprints get collapsed on sight. A fake swarm starves before it spreads, like seedlings at the rim of an oasis with no water, drifting across a wide ocean of cheap registrations, while the verified orchard of long-standing agents keeps its yield.
